Messages.Body:
*** 100 Vampires are coming soon. Please give me some advice on if you
think these cards contain enough untap effects and whether you think
the rarity scheme seems adequate (I'm thinking 1R 3V 3U 4C... weird, I
know, but 2 vamps makes it too tough to draft). As always, comments on
power levels and your own thoughts of cards that would fill anyholes
I've missed in the stereotypical attributes of base sets are
appreciated (specifically the indy disciplines and non-clan/discipline
based stuff). I'm hoping to have this finished in time for an October
Tournament for playtesting. :) ***

Maybe, although both library and crypt selection vary quite a bit in my
draft experience depending on how many good vampires/good library cards
you end up with.

For example, I often play rather less than a 54 card library, maybe more
like 40 to 45, unless I have an awful lot of good library cards for some
reason. Vampire-wise, with existing White Wolf packs (which are 3 vamps
out of 11 cards typically) we do usually end up with a lot more than 12
vampires to choose our crypt from (25-30 on average, I'd say), but this
seems somewhat necessary because of the many vampires that will turn out
not to be optimal for the deck you end up with. That is, the broadness
of a set (or sets) in draft seems to lead to the need for more vampires
to choose from, since the vampires cover X disciplines which you're only
going to be able to use Y of.

2.5 vampires a pack might be more optimal in some sense, but it seems
tricky to do unless you mix vampires and library cards on the same
sheet(s)...

All that said, 1R/3V/2U/5C would make uncommons a little less
common-seeming. That's assuming you don't want to do what some of the
recent WW sets have done and have 1R/3V/7C with no library-card
uncommons.

Josh

Thank you for that.

with the 1.3.X.(7-X) method
Packs----------Crypt---------Library
5 15 40
6 18 48

with the 1.2.Y.(7-Y) method
Packs----------Crypt---------Library
5 10 45
6 12 54

'Your' method requires a purchase of six packs. Better for sales,
perhaps, and of course better for drafting, but the more cards the
better, of course. You're also cutting vampires close, which seems ok,
as you're probably only going to see half of them, but when you get
the one or two that suck a whole lot in your opening crypt hand, its
not like you can use a discard phase action to move on to another
vampire (well... its called four transfers and a pool).

'My' method seems to give extra vampires and not a whole ton of
library cards, but it is at least feasible at the 5 booster pack
level. Cheaper, but really, another three bucks isn't that huge of a
shift. Insert a few Vampire slot library cards to kick the level down
a notch and you're talking business (though the set seems to be
lacking room for anything much less than 98 vampires due to the
multitude of clans contained).

I suppose at this point its pretty much a draw. Some actually
marketting research and drafting playtesting would determine which one
is better.

However, if the rules for drafting were changed to 40 card library
min. and 8 card cypt min... :)

~SV
